ground_truth.title: Top 7 Hot-Swappable Mechanical Keyboards for Beginners
ground_truth.author: Jerry Chu
ground_truth.main_content:
Hot-swappable mechanical keyboards are ideal for beginners because they let you easily change switches without soldering. This flexibility allows you to experiment with different switch types, customize your typing experience, and perform quick repairs. Below are the top 7 beginner-friendly options, each offering unique features and layouts:

Freebird60 Full Kit ($160): Compact 60% layout with CNC aluminum case, QMK/VIA support, and multiple plate options.

Freebird75 Full Kit ($199): 75% layout with dual mounting styles, CNC aluminum build, and hot-swappable PCB.

Freebird TKL Full Kit ($249.99): Tenkeyless layout with customizable mounts and durable aluminum case.

Redragon K530 Draconic ($50): Affordable 60% keyboard with tri-mode wireless connectivity and RGB lighting.

Ajazz AK820 Pro ($58.64): 75% layout with gasket mount, RGB, and integrated TFT display.

Keychron Q2 ($129.99+): 65% aluminum keyboard with a double-gasket design and programmable rotary knob.

Asus ROG Azoth ($229): Premium 75% keyboard with OLED display, tri-mode connectivity, and pre-lubed switches.

Quick Comparison

Keyboard Model Layout Switch Type Connectivity Case Material Price (USD) Key Feature
Freebird60 Full Kit 60% MX-style hot-swap USB-C CNC aluminum $160 QMK/VIA support
Freebird75 Full Kit 75% MX-style hot-swap USB-C CNC aluminum $199 Dual mounting styles
Freebird TKL Full Kit TKL MX-style hot-swap USB-C CNC aluminum $249.99 Top/Gummy O-ring mounts
Redragon K530 Draconic 60% Outemu Box (3/5-pin) USB-C, Bluetooth 5.0, 2.4 GHz ABS plastic $50 Tri-mode wireless
Ajazz AK820 Pro 75% MX-style hot-swap USB-C, Bluetooth 5.1, 2.4 GHz ABS plastic $58.64 Integrated TFT display
Keychron Q2 65% MX-style hot-swap USB-C CNC aluminum $129.99 Double-gasket design
Asus ROG Azoth 75% ROG NX hot-swap USB-C, Bluetooth, 2.4 GHz Metal top cover $229 OLED display, gasket mount

Pick a keyboard based on your preferred layout, budget, and desired features. Hot-swappable models make it easy to personalize your setup and upgrade over time.

Top 5 Hot-Swappable Mechanical Keyboards

Key Features of Beginner Mechanical Keyboards

Look for beginner-friendly features that offer flexibility as you gain experience.

Layout Options

Pick a layout that suits your desk space and typing habits.

Layout Key Features Ideal For
TKL Lacks a numeric keypad but includes full navigation keys Everyday use, gaming
75% Compact design with a function row Productivity, easy to carry
60% Ultra-compact, uses layers for extra functions Saving desk space, travel

Each layout strikes a different balance between functionality and space, making it easier for beginners to find a fit.

Build Quality and Materials

Go for keyboards with solid cases and PBT keycaps. These materials ensure better durability and reduce flex over time.

Hot-Swap Compatibility

Hot-swap sockets allow beginners to easily change switches without the need for soldering, making experimentation much simpler.

Switch Options

Understand the basics of switch types:

Linear: Smooth and quiet

Tactile: Features a noticeable bump when pressed

Clicky: Combines a tactile bump with an audible click

Each type offers a unique typing experience, so try a few to see what feels best.

Ergonomic Considerations

For reduced wrist strain, explore ergonomic features like split designs or tenting options.

With these features in mind, let's dive into the top seven hot-swappable beginner keyboards.

Why Choose a Hot-Swappable Keyboard

Hot-swappable keyboards let you swap out switches without needing to solder, making them a flexible option for beginners and enthusiasts alike.

Experiment with Switches Easily

Trying out different switches is simple. Whether you prefer smooth linear switches for gaming or tactile ones for typing, you can quickly pull out one switch and pop in another to find your perfect match.

Quick Customization

You can change the sound and feel of your keyboard in less than an hour, saving time while personalizing your setup.

Simplified Maintenance and Repairs

Hot-swap keyboards make upkeep a breeze. If a switch stops working, you can replace it in seconds without needing special tools. Soldered keyboards, on the other hand, require desoldering tools and come with the risk of damaging the PCB or switches if not handled carefully.

Tips for Switch Compatibility

Most hot-swappable keyboards support both 3-pin and 5-pin switches, but it’s a good idea to double-check your keyboard’s socket type. Confirming compatibility ahead of time can help you avoid headaches later.

Now that you know the perks, let’s dive into our top hot-swappable keyboard recommendations.

1. Freebird60 Full Kit ( KeebsForAll Exclusive)

The Freebird60 Full Kit is a custom keyboard designed for those stepping into the world of mechanical keyboards. Priced at $160 and weighing 2.03 lb, it offers a 60% layout that combines compactness with a high-quality feel - perfect for beginners looking for a solid starting point.

Features & What's Included

E-coated aluminum case available in Black, Navy, Olive, or White, with a 5° typing angle

FB60 hot-swappable PCB compatible with QMK and VIA

Switch plate options: White POM, Black FR4, or Aluminum

Durock V2 screw-in stabilizers

Silicone dampener and feet for added stability

USB-C connectivity

Rubber O-rings and 2M screws for assembly

The hot-swappable PCB supports all MX-style switches, eliminating the need for soldering. You can easily customize it by adding your favorite switches and keycaps - everything else is included in the kit.

Looking for a slightly larger option? The Freebird75 takes this compact design to the next level with a bigger layout and added programmability.

2. Freebird75 Full Kit (KeebsForAll Exclusive)

The Freebird75 Full Kit takes the popular Freebird60 and upgrades it to a 75% layout, offering a great balance between functionality and desk space. Priced at $199, this kit includes everything you need to build a keyboard - except switches and keycaps.

Build and Design

Crafted with 6063 CNC‑machined aluminum for both the top and bottom case, the Freebird75 measures 12.87" x 5.55" (327 mm x 141 mm) and weighs 5.5 pounds. Its 6° typing angle and 19.5 mm front height are designed for comfortable, fatigue-free typing sessions.

What's Included

Here's what you'll find in the Freebird75 Full Kit:

6063 CNC‑machined aluminum top and bottom case

Hot‑swappable PCB (compatible with QMK & VIA)

Switch plate options: Aluminum, FR4, POM, or PC

C3 Unified Daughterboard with ESD protection

JST cable for connectivity

Silicone case dampener

Carrying case

Mounting hardware: rubber O‑rings for Top Burger Mount, 50A silicone O‑ring gasket for Gummy O‑Ring Mount, and screws

Silicone feet

Customization Features

The Freebird75 offers two mounting styles - Top Burger Mount and Gummy O‑Ring - allowing you to tailor the typing feel to your preference. Choose a firmer, more solid experience or a softer, cushioned response. The hot‑swappable PCB supports both ANSI and ISO layouts, making it versatile for users worldwide.

With full QMK and VIA compatibility, you can easily remap keys and set up macros without needing to code. For even more customization, additional plate materials like brass are available as upgrades. Whether you're new to mechanical keyboards or a seasoned enthusiast, the Freebird75 is built to grow with you.

Looking for something different? Check out the Freebird TKL for a compact layout that's ideal for navigation-focused setups.

3. Freebird TKL Full Kit (KeebsForAll Exclusive)

At $249.99, the Freebird TKL Full Kit is a tenkeyless keyboard designed for easy customization. It features a hot-swappable PCB and a sturdy E-coated CNC aluminum case.

Build Quality and Design

The keyboard is crafted with a CNC-machined aluminum case that’s E-coated for durability. It measures 14.2×5.2×1.6 inches, weighs 4.9 pounds, and has a 6° typing angle. You can choose between WK and WKL layouts for your preferred style.

Features and Components

Case: E-coated CNC aluminum (available in black or white)

PCB: Hot-swappable and compatible with QMK/VIA

Plate Options: Aluminum, POM, FR4, or PC

Mounting Styles: Top Mount or Gummy O-ring

Extras: Durock V2 stabilizers, silicone dampener, silicone feet

Hardware: Includes screws and gummy O-rings

The Top Mount provides a firmer typing experience, while the Gummy O-ring offers a softer, more cushioned feel. With VIA compatibility, you can easily remap keys and set up macros without needing to dive into complex coding.

Next up: check out the affordable Redragon K530 Draconic.

4. Redragon K530 Draconic Review

The Redragon K530 Draconic, priced around $50, is a compact 60% hot-swappable mechanical keyboard. It supports three connectivity options: wired USB-C, Bluetooth 5.0, and 2.4 GHz wireless, all packed into a lightweight plastic case.

This keyboard comes equipped with tactile Outemu Box Brown switches, offering both 3- and 5-pin hot-swap compatibility and a lifespan of up to 50 million keystrokes. It includes ABS double-shot keycaps, per-key RGB backlighting, and a switch puller. Secondary functions are clearly marked with side-printed legends.

Redragon's software allows users to manage macros, customize RGB lighting effects, remap keys, and store profiles. It holds an impressive user rating of 4.8 out of 5 from 81 reviews.

While the ABS keycaps are durable enough for daily use, they lack the premium feel of higher-end keycap sets. Even so, the K530 stands out as a solid entry-level option, thanks to its versatile wireless modes and hot-swappable design.

Next up: 5. Ajazz AK820 Pro Specs.

5. Ajazz AK820 Pro Specs

Priced at $58.64, the Ajazz AK820 Pro is a compact 75% keyboard designed for beginners. It features a gasket-mounted flex-cut PC plate and a sturdy ABS case, offering a comfortable typing experience. Weighing 0.8 kg (1.76 lb), it combines durability with functionality.

Feature Specification
Layout 75% (81 keys + rotary knob)
Switch Type Hot-swappable (3/5-pin compatible)
Keycaps PBT, OEM profile
Dimensions 327 × 136 × 40 mm (12.87 × 5.35 × 1.57 in)
Operating Systems Windows, macOS
Connectivity USB-C, Bluetooth 5.1, 2.4 GHz wireless
Battery 4,000 mAh
Lighting RGB with 1.6 million colors
Screen Integrated TFT display

With an impressive 4.9/5 rating from 42 reviews, it’s clear this keyboard is a hit among users.

Next up: Keychron Q2 Overview.

6. Keychron Q2 Overview

The Keychron Q2 is a solid choice for beginners looking for a high-quality keyboard with excellent build and sound. This 65% mechanical keyboard features a CNC-machined 6063 aluminum body and a double-gasket design that enhances flexibility and sound quality.

Feature Specification
Layout 65%
Body Material CNC-machined 6063 aluminum
Switch Support Hot-swappable (3-pin & 5-pin MX)
Keycaps Double-shot PBT, OSA Profile
Stabilizers Screw-in PCB
Dimensions 11.6 × 4.7 × 1.4 in
Software/Polling QMK/VIA compatible, 1000Hz

The fully assembled version comes with pre-lubed Gateron Pro switches and OSA-profile PBT keycaps.

Key features include:

South-facing RGB LEDs, compatible with Cherry-profile keycaps

Programmable rotary knob (optional)

Mac and Windows compatibility, with extra keycaps included

Full QMK firmware programmability

Pricing starts at $109.99 for the barebone version and $129.99 for the fully assembled one. If you opt for the knob edition, prices are $119.99 and $139.99, respectively.

7. Asus ROG Azoth Features

The Asus ROG Azoth rounds out our list with a premium 75% keyboard that boasts a metal top cover, a silicone gasket mount, and three layers of foam for improved sound quality.

Feature Specification
Layout 75%
Switch Type Hot-swappable ROG NX switches (pre-lubed)
Keycaps ROG PBT doubleshot
Connectivity Tri-mode (2.4 GHz, Bluetooth, USB)
Battery Life Over 2,000 hours (2.4 GHz mode, RGB/OLED off)
Extra Features OLED display, 3 adjustable tilt positions

Inside the box, you'll get pre-lubed ROG NX switches, ROG PBT doubleshot keycaps, and a DIY lube kit that includes an opener, pullers, a station, a brush, and Krytox GPL-205-GD0 lubricant - perfect for customizing your setup. The keyboard's construction features a 3.5 mm silicone pad and a foam-lined base to enhance sound quality. It also supports Tri-mode SpeedNova wireless, Mac and Windows compatibility, Aura Sync RGB, on-the-fly macros, and comes with the ROG Omni Receiver for added convenience.

The Azoth has earned both the Editor's Choice and Best of CES 2023 awards, making it a top-tier option for anyone looking to dive into hot-swappable keyboards. Next, check out how all seven models stack up in the Keyboard Specs at a Glance.

Keyboard Specs at a Glance

Here's a quick comparison of the key specs for our top seven keyboard picks.

Keyboard Model Layout Switch Type Connectivity Case Material Price (USD) Key Feature
Freebird60 Full Kit 60% MX‑style hot‑swap USB‑C CNC aluminum $160 VIA/QMK support
Freebird75 Full Kit 75% MX‑style hot‑swap USB‑C CNC aluminum $199 Dual mounting styles
Freebird TKL Full Kit TKL MX‑style hot‑swap USB‑C CNC aluminum $249.99 Top/Gummy O‑ring mounts
Redragon K530 Draconic 60% Outemu Box (3/5‑pin) USB‑C, Bluetooth 5.0, 2.4 GHz ABS plastic $50 Tri‑mode wireless
Ajazz AK820 Pro 75% MX‑style hot‑swap USB-C, Bluetooth 5.1, 2.4 GHz ABS plastic $58.64 Integrated TFT display
Keychron Q2 65% MX‑style hot‑swap USB‑C CNC aluminum $129.99 Double‑gasket design
Asus ROG Azoth 75% ROG NX hot‑swap USB‑C, Bluetooth, 2.4 GHz Metal top cover $229 OLED display, gasket mount

Picking Your First Hot-Swap Keyboard

Here’s how to find a keyboard that fits your needs.

Size and Layout

Keyboards come in different sizes, so pick one that matches your desk space and how often you use navigation or function keys. Common options include:

TKL (87 keys): A solid choice if you want a compact board but still need dedicated arrow keys and navigation buttons.

75% (80–84 keys): Slightly smaller than TKL but keeps most essential keys.

65% (60–68 keys): Drops the function row and some navigation keys for a smaller footprint.

60% (58–65 keys): Minimalist and compact, but sacrifices most navigation and function keys.

Connection

Decide how you want to connect your keyboard:

Wired (USB-C): Reliable and low-latency, great for gaming or fast typing.

Wireless (Bluetooth or 2.4 GHz): Offers cable-free convenience but may introduce slight lag.

Budget

Your budget will determine the build quality and features:

Under $100: Basic boards with plastic cases, ideal for beginners.

$150–200: Mid-range options with CNC-aluminum builds for better durability and feel.

Over $200: High-end boards with premium materials and customizable mounting options.

Future Upgrades

Hot-swap keyboards let you tweak and customize as you go. You can:

Change out switches and keycaps.

Add features like knobs or custom cables.

Improve comfort with foam inserts or tenting kits.

Starting with a hot-swappable keyboard makes it easy to personalize your setup and fine-tune it over time.

Final Thoughts

Hot-swappable keyboards offer a great mix of convenience and personalization, making them an excellent choice for beginners. Their design lets you try out different switches and handle maintenance with ease - no specialized tools needed.

The Freebird series stands out for its balance of dependability and customization. For example, the Freebird60, priced at $160, comes with a CNC-aluminum case and supports multiple layouts, allowing it to adapt to your preferences over time. When selecting a keyboard, keep your budget and switch compatibility in mind.

While they may have a few limitations compared to soldered boards, hot-swappable keyboards are much easier to maintain and personalize. Check out the "Keyboard Specs at a Glance" section to find the model that best suits your needs.

## Picking Your First Hot-Swap Keyboard

Here’s how to find a keyboard that fits your needs.

### Size and Layout

Keyboards come in different sizes, so pick one that matches your desk space and how often you use navigation or function keys. Common options include:

**TKL (87 keys)**: A solid choice if you want a compact board but still need dedicated arrow keys and navigation buttons.

**75% (80–84 keys)**: Slightly smaller than TKL but keeps most essential keys.

**65% (60–68 keys)**: Drops the function row and some navigation keys for a smaller footprint.

**60% (58–65 keys)**: Minimalist and compact, but sacrifices most navigation and function keys.

### Connection

Decide how you want to connect your keyboard:

**Wired (USB-C)**: Reliable and low-latency, great for gaming or fast typing.

**Wireless (Bluetooth or 2.4 GHz)**: Offers cable-free convenience but may introduce slight lag.

### Budget

Your budget will determine the build quality and features:

**Under $100**: Basic boards with plastic cases, ideal for beginners.

**$150–200**: Mid-range options with CNC-aluminum builds for better durability and feel.

**Over $200**: High-end boards with premium materials and customizable mounting options.

### Future Upgrades

Hot-swap keyboards let you tweak and customize as you go. You can:

Change out switches and keycaps.

Add features like knobs or custom cables.

Improve comfort with foam inserts or tenting kits.

Starting with a [hot-swappable keyboard](https://keebsforall.com/en-ca/products/s46-keyboard) makes it easy to personalize your setup and fine-tune it over time.

## Final Thoughts

[Hot-swappable keyboards](https://keebsforall.com/products/s46-keyboard) offer a great mix of convenience and personalization, making them an excellent choice for beginners. Their design lets you [try out different switches](https://keebsforall.com/collections/keyboard-switches/nlandkeys) and handle maintenance with ease - no specialized tools needed.

The [Freebird series](https://keebsforall.com/collections/freebird-series) stands out for its balance of dependability and customization. For example, the Freebird60, priced at $160, comes with a CNC-aluminum case and supports multiple layouts, allowing it to adapt to your preferences over time. When selecting a keyboard, keep your budget and switch compatibility in mind.

While they may have a few limitations compared to soldered boards, hot-swappable keyboards are much easier to maintain and personalize. Check out the "Keyboard Specs at a Glance" section to find the model that best suits your needs.
